input.purpose: Measure the scrubber-served Lab air volume V_lab from the CO2 decay time constant and known effective scrubber flow.
hypotheses: The Lab is a single well-mixed zone during both phases.
The closed /habitat/lab/hatch-1-v7 has negligible exchange with /habitat/hab-b during the fit; closed-opening exchange is not measured by this test.
The three named Lab occupants remain in the Lab at steady activity throughout; any entry, exit, or added occupant invalidates the curve.
The scrubber effective flow scales with commanded speed and its registered full-speed effective flow is valid.
The Lab CO2 sensor records at one-minute intervals, while the connected Hab-B CO2 sensor is recorded at the same interval to reveal inter-zone exchange.

monitoring.reason: The reduced-flow phase intentionally raises the CO2 breathed by the three Lab occupants; abort on an out-of-band vital sign, monitoring loss, or occupancy change.

steps.why: Hold the Lab as one zone and reduce effective flow long enough for occupant CO2 to rise several hundred ppm above sensor noise, without exceeding the written limit.
Keep the same zone boundary, restore full flow, record one-minute Lab and Hab-B CO2 plus command acceptance, and fit the decay toward its nonzero equilibrium.

abort.when: Lab CO2 is at or above 3000 ppm.
The scrubber refuses either commanded speed.
Scrubber battery state of charge is under 35 percent.
Any monitored subject is outside 45–120 bpm, monitoring is lost, or any additional person is present in the Lab.

expected.rise: From the measured 1050 ppm start, Lab CO2 should rise by several hundred ppm during the 30 percent phase while remaining below 2800 ppm; failure to rise above sensor noise challenges the source or flow-scaling hypotheses.
expected.decay: After the command to 100 percent, Lab CO2 should follow C(t)=C_eq+(C_0-C_eq)exp(-t/tau), fitted toward a nonzero equilibrium rather than zero or outdoor concentration.
expected.volume: Compute V_lab=Qe*tau using the scrubber's registered full-speed effective flow Qe and the fitted decay time constant tau; report the fit interval, uncertainty, and residuals.
expected.opening_check: Hab-B CO2 should not show a synchronous complementary response. A correlated Lab/Hab-B change indicates material exchange through the closed hatch and invalidates the one-zone/negligible-exchange hypothesis.
expected.validity: Any occupant entry or exit, activity change, refused speed command, safety abort, non-exponential residual structure, or failure to obtain a rise of several hundred ppm makes the volume result invalid and requires a revised test.
